page: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance allocates 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core on a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor. It features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction set support includes AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes an 81 GB local SSD for high-speed temporary storage and contains no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the constraints of its two-thread, single-core configuration. While single-threaded tests yield mid-tier performance—such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1581.0, gzip compression throughput of 28.16 GB/sec, and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1889.99—multi-threaded workloads place in the lowest percentiles. Geekbench multi-core achieved 1866.0, PassMark CPU reached 2986.33, and stress-ng multi-core logged 1932.99, all placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show 14.72 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 13.46 GB/sec for writes.

With its 81 GB bundled local SSD and solid single-thread performance, the D2ds_v5 offers standard entry-tier efficiency for small footprints that benefit from local scratch space without paying for multi-core density. However, overall throughput remains limited for parallel computing. It is suited for basic web serving, small databases, developer testing, continuous integration build agents, and microservices with moderate traffic.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v5 is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs backed by 1 dedicated physical core, 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), and an 81 GB local SSD, with no hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate competitive single-core execution—scoring 1581.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1889.99 in stress-ng—but low multi-threaded and memory throughput due to the dual-thread ceiling. PassMark CPU reached 2986.33, while Redis SET operations peaked at 1.93 million operations per second. The server offers cost-effective compute capacity for low-scale environments needing fast local scratch disks, making it suitable for lightweight web applications, microservices, background processing tasks, and testing environments.
